title: African Mahogany: Ancient African Mahoganies You Can Visit
meta_description: A West African tree that does better abroad. Rio's reaches 49.1 metres, and Florida's state champion has a crown wider than it is tall.
intro: African mahogany is a tree of the West African savanna that stops at around 30 to 35 metres in the wild, and outside its range it has sometimes done better. In Rio de Janeiro's Jardim Botanico, one reaches 49.1 metres, the tallest tree in the garden's living collection and the anchor of its Giant Trees Trail. In Plantation, Florida, the state champion was measured in June 2024 at 4.17 metres round and 28 metres tall, with a crown 38 metres across, wider than the tree is high. In Singapore, Lee Kuan Yew planted one beside Swan Lake on 2 November 1980, and it is now 5.7 metres round and 25 metres tall. The species is scarce back in West Africa, where its timber is worked hard and governments restrict its export.
